claims.text: Forty-one percent of eligible adult patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation were sarcopenic.
Sarcopenia is significantly more prevalent in males than females among patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation.
Sarcopenia prevalence increases with higher Child-Pugh class in patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation.
Male sex, dry-weight body mass index, and Child-Pugh class C cirrhosis are independent predictors of sarcopenia in patients listed for liver transplantation.
Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score is not an independent predictor of sarcopenia in patients listed for liver transplantation.
Sarcopenia is an independent predictor of waiting-list mortality after adjustments for age and MELD scores in patients listed for liver transplantation.
Sarcopenia is poorly predicted by subjective nutritional assessment tools such as body mass index and subjective global assessment.

evidence.description: Forty-one percent of the 142 eligible patients were sarcopenic.
Sarcopenia was more prevalent in males versus females (54% versus 21%, P < 0.001).
Sarcopenia increased with the Child-Pugh class (10% for class A, 34% for class B, and 54% for class C, P = 0.007).
Male sex, the dry-weight body mass index (BMI), and Child-Pugh class C cirrhosis (but not the MELD score) were independent predictors of sarcopenia.
Male sex, the dry-weight body mass index (BMI), and Child-Pugh class C cirrhosis (but not the MELD score) were independent predictors of sarcopenia.
Sarcopenia was an independent predictor of mortality (hazard ratio = 2.36, 95% confidence interval = 1.23-4.53) after adjustments for age and MELD scores.
Sarcopenia is poorly predicted by subjective nutritional assessment tools such as BMI and subjective global assessment.

methodologies.name: Retrospective cohort study using cross-sectional imaging
methodologies.description: Retrospective identification and analysis of adults listed for liver transplantation who underwent abdominal CT or MRI within 6 weeks of activation to evaluate sarcopenia prevalence, predictors, and waiting-list mortality.
conditions: Adults listed for liver transplantation with abdominal CT/MRI within 6 weeks of activation
Excluded listing for multivisceral transplantation or living related liver transplantation

limitations.text: The findings require validation in larger studies.

future_work.text: Validation of objective sarcopenia assessment in larger studies for prognostication in liver transplant candidates.
